zh: 我们已经在播客上邀请过 Ben Mann 和 Mike Krieger,他们现在都在 Labs 工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: Talk about Labs.
zh: 谈谈 Labs 吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is Labs?
zh: Labs 是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: What's come out of Labs?
zh: 从 Labs 中诞生了什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Many people have heard of these things.
zh: 许多人已经听说过这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And how do they work that enables them to create such innovative ideas outside of even the core Anthropic product team?
zh: 以及它们是如何运作的,使得它们甚至能够在核心 Anthropic 产品团队之外创造出如此创新的想法?

speaker: Unknown
en: The thesis of Labs in many ways is identifying and pulling the thread on...
zh: Labs 的论点在很多方面是识别并拉扯这根线索关于……

speaker: Unknown
en: ... in many ways is identifying and pulling the thread on the thread of discontinuous large bets that might not be in the core roadmap, and figuring out is there a there there?
zh: ……在很多方面是识别并拉扯这根线索关于那些可能不在核心路线图上的非连续性大型押注的线索,并弄清楚那里是否有实质内容?

speaker: Unknown
en: And also, what is the 10X, 100X, 1000X of the there there?
zh: 而且,那个实质内容的 10 倍、100 倍、1000 倍是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for example, things like Claude Code, I think-
zh: 所以例如,像 Claude Code 这样的东西,我想——

speaker: Unknown
en: I've heard of it.
zh: 我听说过它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Things like Claude Code, things like skills, and most recently Claude Design, MCP.
zh: 像 Claude Code 这样的东西,像 skills 这样的东西,以及最近的 Claude Design,MCP。

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing that we really try to emphasize within the teams is, especially right now, there are so many things that could be built.
zh: 我们在团队内部真正努力强调的是,特别是现在,有太多可以构建的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does it mean then to have a discontinuous bet?
zh: 那么拥有一个不连续的赌注意味着什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think one approach that we're taking this year is you can be very strongly held opinion about the theme or the area, and then more weakly held about the exact prototype.
zh: 我认为我们今年采取的一种方法是,你可以对一个主题或一个领域持有非常强烈的观点,然后对确切的原型持有较弱的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's a culture of experimentation.
zh: 因此存在一种实验的文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of the bottoms up engineers on the team are very self-enabled, self-driven to test out different ideas.
zh: 有很多团队中自下而上的工程师非常自我赋能、自我驱动地去测试不同的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: And sometimes, we have a thesis, and it might not work yet, and so we then might revisit it in one to two model generations.
zh: 有时候,我们有一个论点,它可能暂时还不可行,因此我们可能会在一到两个 model 世代后重新审视它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this idea of these prototypes that actually end up just helping us learn, that's also valuable even if it doesn't lead to something immediately shipping.
zh: 因此这些最终只是帮助我们学习的原型的想法,那也是有价值的,即使它不能立即导向某些交付的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think that allows the incubation and the charter of Labs to really accelerate and see around corners more broadly for Anthropic.
zh: 因此我认为这允许 Labs 的孵化和使命真正加速,并为 Anthropic 更广泛地预见未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's so funny to think about Labs within an Anthropic, which was already so innovative and creative and just shipping like crazy, that there's value to still creating a Labs team within Anthropic.
zh: 想到在 Anthropic 内部的 Labs 是如此有趣,Anthropic 本身已经如此创新和有创造力,并且疯狂地交付,但仍然在 Anthropic 内部创建一个 Labs 团队仍然有价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: What enables Labs to work as well as it has?
zh: 是什么让 Labs 能够像它一直以来那样出色地运作?

speaker: Unknown
en: Because you listed all these products and it's like, what else has Anthropic shipped?
zh: 因为你列出了所有这些产品,这就像,Anthropic 还交付了什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels like all the biggest wins almost.
zh: 感觉几乎所有的最大胜利都是。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sure there are many that I'm not thinking about right now.
zh: 我确定有很多我现在没有想到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's core to creating a successful Labs org within a larger company?
zh: 在一个更大的公司内创建一个成功的 Labs 组织的核心是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the team culture, similar to broadly at Anthropic, I think the team culture is very valuable.
zh: 我认为团队文化,类似于 Anthropic 总体上的情况,我认为团队文化非常有价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Ben sets an incredible vision and pushes people to think about the 10X, 100X of the idea.
zh: 我认为 Ben 设定了一个令人难以置信的愿景,并推动人们去思考想法的 10 倍、100 倍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the teams, the pods within Labs is small, sometimes these ideas start with one engineer.
zh: 而且 Labs 内部的团队、这些小集群是很小的,有时这些想法从一个工程师开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think sometimes when there's almost really large teams pursuing very ambiguous large ideas, you end up actually being slowed down because of that.
zh: 我认为有时候当有几乎非常大的团队追求非常模糊的宏大想法时,你最终实际上反而因此被拖慢了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think it's culture.
zh: 所以我认为是文化。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we actually also select for folks who actually want to do that zero to one experimentation.
zh: 我认为我们实际上也在筛选那些真正想做那种从零到一实验的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's not easy.
zh: 这并不容易。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of bets that we end up turning down or turning off.
zh: 有很多赌注我们最终拒绝了或关闭了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And maybe we revisit them in the future, but that's hard.
zh: 也许我们未来会重新审视它们,但那很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's hard when you pour your heart and soul, you're acting as a founder for a bet and it's not working yet.
zh: 当你倾注了你全部的心血和灵魂,你作为一个赌注的创始人行事,而它暂时还不可行时,那是很难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think it's like that type, it's selecting for that type of personality, folks who are really passionate and deep about the zero to one.
zh: 所以我认为就是那种类型,就是筛选那种类型的人格,那些对从零到一真正充满激情和深度的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you lead product for the research team, you work with the researchers at Anthropic.
zh: 所以你领导研究团队的产品,你与 Anthropic 的研究人员一起工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of people get a sense of what is research.
zh: 很多人对什么是研究有一种感觉。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do researchers do?
zh: 研究人员做什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot of people don't totally understand these very valuable people at all the AI labs.
zh: 我认为很多人并不完全理解所有 AI 实验室里这些非常有价值的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: The way I think about it, and I want to help people understand, help me understand just what are researchers doing all day.
zh: 我思考它的方式是,我想帮助人们理解,帮我理解研究人员整天都在做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I imagine is they have a hypothesis for how to improve the model.
zh: 我想象的是他们对如何改进模型有一个假设。

speaker: Unknown
en: They find data, they tweak some algorithms, they adjust how it's trained, and they test it, see how it did, keep iterating and keep trying to find ways to improve the model.
zh: 他们寻找数据,他们调整一些算法,他们调整它的训练方式,然后他们测试它,看它表现得如何,不断迭代,并不断尝试找到改进模型的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that roughly right?
zh: 这大致正确吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Slash help us understand what researchers are doing all day.
zh: 斜杠帮助我们理解研究人员整天都在做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's a lot of maybe the more day-to-day.
zh: 我认为那可能是更多日常的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think one piece around researchers and research organizations like at Anthropic is there's also a vision of the future more broadly.
zh: 我认为关于像 Anthropic 这样的研究人员和研究组织的一个方面是,还有一个更宏大的关于未来的愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, things like, I think even at the founding of the company, researchers were talking about how do we get Claude to use a computer?
zh: 所以例如,这样的事情,我认为甚至在公司成立时,研究人员就在谈论我们如何让 Claude 使用一台计算机?

speaker: Unknown
en: How do we get AI to navigate a screen?
zh: 我们如何让 AI 导航一个屏幕?

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's a lot of actually very founder-like energy is how I describe it within researchers are really bold and ambitious researchers, and we have a ton of those at Anthropic.
zh: 所以实际上有很多非常像创始人的能量,这是我对研究人员的描述,他们是非常大胆和雄心勃勃的研究人员,而我们在 Anthropic 有大量这样的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's one layer of vision of what this technology can go.
zh: 所以有一层关于这项技术能走到哪里的愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I think on this other side of the loop, there's also, now that this technology or Claude is in people's hands, how do we make it better today?
zh: 然后我认为在循环的另一面,也有,既然这项技术或 Claude 已经在人们手中,我们今天如何让它变得更好?

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's a medium and long-term, and a lot of energy thinking about that lens of the future.
zh: 所以它是中期和长期的,有很多能量在思考那个未来的视角。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also, in the immediate and short term, what are the improvement areas we can make?
zh: 而且同样,在当下和短期内,我们可以做出哪些改进领域?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think you're describing a really good sense of how do we make iterative improvements on different versions of Claude?
zh: 因此我认为你描述了一种非常好的感觉,关于我们如何对 Claude 的不同版本进行迭代改进?

speaker: Unknown
en: The way that my team works with researchers is being very integrated and embedded in those loops, particularly areas where there's a lot of impact on users.
zh: 我的团队与研究人员合作的方式是高度整合并嵌入到这些循环中,特别是在对用户有大量影响的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is things like vision, computer use, coding, agentic coding, tool use, test time compute, things where there's a direct user impact.
zh: 所以这些事情像是视觉、计算机使用、编码、智能体编码、工具使用、测试时计算,这些有直接用户影响的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then figuring out what are the ways to bring the user feedback, and ground it in a level that is understandable for researchers, and also actionable for researchers.
zh: 然后找出有哪些方法可以带来用户反馈,并将其落实到一个对研究人员来说可理解、也可操作的层面上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's the second piece is actually a big part of the job and sometimes a hard part of the job.
zh: 而且我认为这第二部分实际上构成了工作的很大一部分,有时也是工作中困难的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, we might get feedback on claude.ai.
zh: 所以例如,我们可能会在 claude.ai 上收到反馈。

speaker: Unknown
en: "Claude hallucinated."
zh: "Claude 产生了幻觉。"

speaker: Unknown
en: It's very vague.
zh: 这非常模糊。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you bring that to a researcher and you say, "Please fix Claude from being hallucinated," it's not very actionable.
zh: 如果你把这个交给一位研究员然后说,"请修复 Claude 产生幻觉的问题,"这并不是非常可操作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so part of the time of the team is understanding, okay, what's the trajectory of why that user gave that feedback?
zh: 所以团队的一部分时间是在理解,好的,为什么那个用户给了那个反馈的轨迹是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's consented.
zh: 而且这是经过同意的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we look at, okay, what should Claude have called tools in that moment?
zh: 所以我们看的是,好的,在那个时刻 Claude 本应该调用什么工具?

speaker: Unknown
en: Or from its current knowledge or it looked at the right document, but it looked at the wrong facts.
zh: 或者是从它当前的知识来看,或者它看了正确的文档,但它看了错误的事实。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the first case, that would have been a failure on tool use.
zh: 在第一种情况下,那会是工具使用上的失败。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the second case, it would've been a failure on, let's say, search or knowledge insertion, search synthesis, or it could be something around alignment.
zh: 在第二种情况下,比如说会是搜索或知识插入、搜索综合上的失败,或者可能是某种关于对齐的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so bring that level of detail to researchers coming up with, is this a big enough problem?
zh: 所以把这种程度的细节带给研究员们来得出,这是一个足够大的问题吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Figure out things like evals to then describe what we've improved it.
zh: 找出像 evals 这样的事情来然后描述我们改进了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are the levels of actionability, and it's the day-to-day language of their researchers.
zh: 那些就是可操作性的层级,而这是他们研究员的日常语言。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we try to stay very close to how to bring that in an actionable manner between users to the core model training and the research development loop.
zh: 所以我们试图保持非常贴近如何以可操作的方式在用户与核心模型训练以及研发循环之间将其引入。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was talking to someone the other day about how it feels like AI research is the place to be now if you want to be very successful in life.
zh: 我前几天和某个人在聊,感觉如果你想在人生中非常成功的话,AI 研究是现在该去的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does it take to become a really successful researcher from which you can tell?
zh: 从你所能看出的来说,成为一个真正成功的研究员需要什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Not everyone's brain is going to work this way, but just say people are like, "Hey, I want to explore this career path."
zh: 不是每个人的大脑都会这样运作,但就是说人们会说,"嘿,我想探索这条职业路径。"

speaker: Unknown
en: From what you've seen, what does it take to make it there?
zh: 从你所看到的来看,要走到那一步需要什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Researchers generally, or research and product managers working with research, or both?
zh: 总的来说是指研究员,还是与研究合作的产品经理,还是两者都是?

speaker: Lenny
en: Let's do both.
zh: 两个都谈吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the researchers, PMs working with researchers also going to be very successful, but it feels like everyone's trying to poach all the top researchers across every company.
zh: 但是研究员们,与研究员合作的 PM 们也会非常成功,但感觉每个人都在试图从每家公司挖走所有顶尖的研究员。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I know you're not an AI researcher, but just from what you've seen, just what does it take to make it in that career path?
zh: 所以我知道你不是 AI 研究员,但仅从你所看到的来看,要在那条职业路径上取得成功需要什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot of the most successful researchers and research leadership at Anthropic are folks who are really strong first principles thinkers about problems.
zh: 我认为在 Anthropic 许多最成功的研究员和研究领导层是对问题真正强大的第一性原理思考者。

speaker: Unknown
en: They reason through problems really well, who are just passionate about their research area and have a bold description of what that could look like.
zh: 他们非常好地推理问题,对自己的研究领域充满热情,并对那可能是什么样子有大胆的描述。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then who are actually close to the details.
zh: 然后是那些实际上贴近细节的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so our leadership, our chief scientists, our heads of fine-tuning and RL, folks are actually really close to the training runs and actually look at things like how the training run is going, evals, looking at the underlying data.
zh: 所以我们的领导层,我们的首席科学家,我们负责微调和 RL 的人,实际上非常贴近训练运行,并且实际上在看诸如训练运行进展如何、evals、查看底层数据这些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So actually staying really close and be excited to be in the details, I think have been a sign of really strong researchers and developing taste.
zh: 所以实际上保持非常贴近并乐于深入细节,我认为一直是真正强大的研究员和培养品味的标志。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think another piece is just their ability to think big over time and be very ambitious.
zh: 而且我认为另一个方面就是他们随着时间推移能够想得宏大并且非常雄心勃勃的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like the Dario, like we can transform software engineering.
zh: 就像 Dario 那样,就像我们可以改变软件工程一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think going in that direction, you learn so much.
zh: 而且我认为朝着那个方向前进,你会学到很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to shoot for the stars in many ways across your ideas, I think, in order to be a successful researcher.
zh: 我认为你必须在很多方面对你的想法志存高远,才能成为一个成功的研究员。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love just this meme of just be more ambitious comes up so often now, which is so hard.
zh: 我就是喜欢这个"只要更雄心勃勃"的梗现在经常出现,这太难了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's easy to say that it's hard to actually just like how big can you think, and how that's so much of what AI now unlocks, just be more ambitious.
zh: 说起来容易,实际上很难,就像你能想多大,而这很大程度上就是 AI 现在所解锁的,只要更雄心勃勃。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's thinking through it once or twice end-to-end.
zh: 我认为这是从头到尾思考一遍或两遍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then being, I think, stubborn about the area and maybe more loose around the exact approach.
zh: 然后是,我认为,对领域的固执,也许在具体方法上更松散。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is a question we challenge ourselves with, but the technology is moving so quickly, and so how do you make sure what you're building is actually forward compatible?
zh: 这是一个我们不断挑战自己的问题,但技术发展得如此之快,所以你如何确保你正在构建的东西实际上是向前兼容的?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's also actually part of, I think, the core product development loop to think bigger.
zh: 所以这实际上也是,我认为,核心产品研发循环中想得更大的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: One thing I ask the team frequently or how I think about when we're building a product is let's say Claude 8 comes around.
zh: 我经常问团队的一件事,或者我在我们构建产品时的思考方式是,假设 Claude 8 出现了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What changes in what users do?
zh: 用户所做的事情会发生什么变化?

speaker: Unknown
en: And then what does that mean for how you're building today?
zh: 然后这对今天你如何构建意味着什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it going to be forward compatible to that experience?
zh: 它对于那个体验会是向前兼容的吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: So just grounding, I think being ambitious is very broad.
zh: 所以只是落地,我认为雄心勃勃是非常宽泛的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so trying to ground it in some ways of describing that.
zh: 所以试图以某种方式来落地描述它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And also, yeah, everything heading in a direction that all is cohesive and makes sense versus just ambitious in a completely different direction.
zh: 而且,是的,一切都朝着协调一致且有意义的方向前进,而不是在一个完全不同的方向上雄心勃勃。

speaker: Unknown
en: Speaking of ambition and Claude 8, Fable/Mythos recently feels like hit this very new tipping point with models where it used to be you have an awesome model, release it.
zh: 说到雄心和 Claude 8,Fable/Mythos 最近感觉达到了模型的一个非常新的临界点,以前的情况是你有一个很棒的模型,发布它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey everyone, welcome.
zh: 大家好,欢迎。

speaker: Unknown
en: Opus 4.5 is out.
zh: Opus 4.5 发布了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Everyone can use it.
zh: 每个人都可以使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mythos went in a very different direction.
zh: Mythos 走向了一个非常不同的方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: We got blocked.
zh: 我们被封锁了。

speaker: Unknown
en: There was a lot of scrutiny, a lot of concern about what it was capable of.
zh: 有大量的审查,大量的关于它能够做什么的担忧。

speaker: Unknown
en: All the companies had to go make sure it wasn't going to hack into all their systems.
zh: 所有公司都不得不去确保它不会黑进他们所有的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it feels like now every model, because they continue to get better, will now have a lot more scrutiny and there'll be more restrictions on who can use them, which feels like a big deal.
zh: 而且感觉现在每个模型,因为它们继续变得更好,现在都会有更多的审查,并且在谁可以使用它们方面会有更多的限制,这感觉像是一件大事。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about that?
zh: 你怎么看待这件事?

speaker: Unknown
en: How does that change the way you operate?
zh: 这如何改变你运营的方式?

speaker: Unknown

zh: 而对于我的研究产品经理团队来说,驱动用户价值的方法是找出正确的用户反馈,以及能够体现这种用户需求的评估。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: Was this Claude being overconfident?
zh: 这是 Claude 过度自信了吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: So the theme of the failure actually has a lot of nuance, and then that allows you to build a description, a sustained description of that pain point.
zh: 所以失败的主题实际上有很多细微差别,然后这就允许你构建一个描述,一个关于那个痛点的持续描述。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's just the actionability and shorten the distance to actionability for our stakeholders and partner teams like researchers to take action on.

speaker: Unknown
en: Is there an example of something like this where you found an issue or opportunity and then wrote the eval?

en: And so then we added that to our repositories for evals, and when we have versions of Claude, we actually run that eval and just check.

speaker: Unknown
